channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: The latest: Wild’s Quinn Hughes scores OT winner for U.S. to beat Sweden in men’s hockey quarterfinal
item.description: Canada and Finland also needed overtime Wednesday to advance to the semifinals at the Milan Cortina Olympics. Team USA will play Slovakia next on Friday.

item.title: Gophers women’s basketball takes down No. 10 Ohio State for ninth straight win
item.description: Sophie Hart had 18 points and 10 rebounds in the victory, while Amaya Battle had five assists to move into second place on the Gophers’ all-time leaderboard.

item.title: Renee Good memorial site in south Minneapolis doused in gasoline
item.description: Damage from a burning pile of wood was minimal but police are investigating.

item.title: Minnesota released a report about social services fraud. Most of it is blacked out.
item.description: The Department of Human Services said the redactions are to protect trade secrets and security information. Lawmakers looking for answers to state government’s fraud problems are frustrated.

item.title: Moriarty: State ‘in good shape’ to consider charging federal agents in slayings of Good, Pretti
item.description: Lacking federal help, Hennepin prosecutor expresses confidence in state evidence from deaths of Renee Good and Alex Pretti.

item.title: Hennepin County says it released voter data in error. Republicans are using it to demand more.
item.description: Republicans are using the data to put pressure on state officials to comply with a demand from the federal government to see the state’s entire voter rolls.

item.title: St. Paul law firm, famous for clergy sex abuse cases, snared in data breach
item.description: Jeff Anderson & Associates paid a ransom to the hacker in turn for guarantees that the data would be destroyed.

item.title: St. Paul bans ICE face coverings, requires identifying badges
item.description: The ordinance requires law enforcement, including ICE and Customs and Border Protection agents, to work without identity-obscuring masks.

item.title: Minnesota snowstorm mires traffic in Twin Cities and brings power failures in Arrowhead region
item.description: The National Weather Service reported a snowfall total of more than two inches at the Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport and more than four inches in Chanhassen.

item.title: ‘Please come back’: Minnesota restaurants brace for a long recovery after ICE surge
item.description: With no official bailout on the horizon, the restaurant community tries to save itself.
